projects.locationName: Maxella Ave & Glencoe Ave, Marina Del Rey, CA

projects.title: THOUGHTHOUSE
projects.locationName: Full Square Urban Block, West Los Angeles, CA
projects.summary: A hybrid sanctuary in the round sited on an isolated city block surrounded by streets on all four sides. Derived through analytic geometry from Stuart Davis's 'Egg Beater No. 2', the project balances intimate seclusion and shared worship through dramatic conical apertures and acoustic surfaces.

projects.title: Roland Exhibition Pavilion (Polyphonic Tectonics)
projects.locationName: Anaheim Convention Center, Hall A-B, Anaheim, CA
projects.summary: An inward-imploding acoustic sanctuary sited directly on the noisy trade show floor of the Anaheim Convention Center for NAMM. Rejecting standard pipe-and-drape convention carpet culture, the pavilion uses extruded 6061-T6 aluminum truss frames and basalt rockwool baffles to achieve -34 dB isolation, offering visitors an uncanny acoustic vacuum to test classic analog synthesizers.

projects.title: Cut to Connect (Karma Borgo di Colleoli)
projects.typology: Historic Borgo Adaptive Reuse & Landscape Intervention
projects.locationName: Karma Borgo di Colleoli, Palaia, Tuscany, Italy
projects.summary: Our site strategy proposal for Karma Borgo di Colleoli is formulated to create spaces of connection through selective surgical incisions into the historic fabric. The winery proposal at the south end bridges across the provincial road like a vine, co-opting the ideal of the Corridoio Vasariano and Ponte Vecchio in nearby Florence into a living gallery and panoramic viewing concourse. The pinwheel morphology connects the southern pressing/aging root with the northern tasting pavilions and hillside vineyard suites, threading terraced landscape amphitheaters into the topography.

uhi_research_sites.title: Altadena Regrowth: Bioremediation, Mycelium & Seeds
uhi_research_sites.subtitle: Altadena Wildland-Urban Interface • Spring 2026
uhi_research_sites.typology: Interactive Sonic Thick Map, Bioacoustic Soundwalk & Mycoremediation
uhi_research_sites.summary: An interactive sonic thick map and community poetic exercise conducted along the Altadena wildland-urban interface at the foot of the San Gabriel Mountains. Partnering with local environmental justice groups, the project investigates post-wildfire ecological rebirth, heavy metal soil contamination, native chaparral fire-follower seed germination, and mycoremediation via Pleurotus ostreatus (oyster mushroom) fungal networks.
notes: Mycoremediation Plots: Testing oyster mushroom mycelial mats along stormwater runoff swales to break down petroleum hydrocarbons.
Chaparral Seed Banks: Spatial mapping of fire-adapted native seed regeneration (Ceanothus, Arctostaphylos) across burned slopes.
Sonic Thick Map Soundwalk: Field recordings capturing subterranean soil moisture sensors, wind through scorched sage, and community verse readings.

uhi_research_sites.title: Sonic Thick Maps of Valleys: Hawaii Supermarket
uhi_research_sites.subtitle: Valley Blvd & Del Mar Ave, San Gabriel • Fall 2025
uhi_research_sites.summary: Multi-sensory ethnography centered on Hawaii Supermarket at the intersection of Valley Boulevard and Del Mar Avenue in San Gabriel. Using binaural field recording and decibel spectrogram mapping, this research reveals the rich acoustic ecology of the San Gabriel Valley Asian diaspora commercial corridor: cart wheels rattling over weathered asphalt, seafood aerator hums, bilingual price calls, and the contrasting sonic buffer between six-lane vehicular arterials and sheltered dining courtyards.
notes: Binaural Market Aisle Recordings: Dynamic audio capture of produce misting nozzles, cleaver rhythms, and polyglot exchanges.
Valley Blvd Arterial Buffer: Decibel attenuation analysis demonstrating how courtyard architecture buffers 78 dB traffic roar down to 54 dB conversational calm.
Sensory Thick Mapping: Synthesizing aromas, acoustic envelopes, and diaspora memory into layered spatial drawings.

uhi_research_sites.title: Savoring the City: Hispanic & Latino Culinary Geographies
uhi_research_sites.subtitle: In Partnership with Los Angeles Public Library • Summer 2025
uhi_research_sites.typology: Archival Cartography, Oral Histories & Culinary Preservation
uhi_research_sites.summary: A spatial research and public archive initiative conducted in direct collaboration with the Los Angeles Public Library Special Collections. Investigating the cultural geographies of Hispanic and Latino restaurants, panaderias, and street vending corridors across East Los Angeles, Boyle Heights, and Pico-Union, the project georeferences historical menus, maps culinary migration paths, and records oral histories of intergenerational food establishments.
notes: LAPL Culinary Archive Digitization: Geocoding historic menus from 1940–2020 to map the evolution of regional Mexican and Central American foodways.
Oral History Cartography: Multi-generational video and audio interviews with legacy restaurant owners facing gentrification pressures.
Zoning & Street Vendor Networks: Spatial policy analysis of sidewalk vending zones, commissary kitchen access, and community nourishment.

field_studies_italy.title: Florence (Firenze) — Consolidated Architecture Dossier
field_studies_italy.subtitle: Piazza del Duomo, Santa Maria Novella, San Lorenzo
field_studies_italy.typology: Renaissance Tectonics, Civic Piazzas & Urban Fabric
field_studies_italy.summary: Comprehensive urban and architectural field survey of Florence across the final two days of the UCLA travel studio. Rather than splintering into isolated dots, this consolidated metropolitan dossier documents the key Renaissance monuments and street networks visited: Santa Maria del Fiore, Santa Maria Novella, the Basilica di San Lorenzo, and the surrounding historic fabric.
notes: Santa Maria del Fiore: Brunelleschi's double-shell masonry dome constructed without centering scaffolding using herringbone brickwork (spina di pesce) and stone chain tension rings.
Santa Maria Novella: Leon Battista Alberti's iconic 1470 marble Renaissance facade—a profound study in harmonic Euclidean proportions, classical volutes, and polychrome marble revetment.
Basilica di San Lorenzo: Brunelleschi's early Renaissance nave proportions, Michelangelo's Laurentian Library vestibule with theatrical cascade stairs, and the Medici Chapels.
Urban Fabric & Sustenance: Walking survey through historic street canyons, terminating at Tomaso's / Vini e Vecchi Sapori for authentic Florentine studio lunches.

field_studies_italy.title: Tenuta Ammiraglia — Frescobaldi
field_studies_italy.subtitle: Magliano in Toscana, Maremma • Arch. Piero Sartogo
field_studies_italy.summary: Tuesday morning field trip into the rolling hills of Maremma. Designed by Piero Sartogo, Tenuta Ammiraglia resembles an aerodynamic naval vessel gliding along the topography. Its 130-meter slit cantilever roof is embedded with natural vegetation, shading fermentation facilities and blending the industrial gravity-flow process seamlessly into the coastal Mediterranean landscape.
notes: Cantilever Blade: 130-meter thin structural roof slit resembling an ocean liner sailing the hills.
Gravity Winemaking: 3-tier vertical production matrix allowing gentle gravity-fed grape handling.
Environmental Envelope: Extensive green roof providing passive thermal insulation against Maremma heat.

field_studies_italy.title: Rocca di Frassinello
field_studies_italy.subtitle: Gavorrano, Maremma • Arch. Renzo Piano
field_studies_italy.summary: Tuesday afternoon field trip exploring Renzo Piano's seminal Tuscan winery. Piano conceived the facility as a subterranean amphitheater: an enormous 40x40 meter square hall holding 2,500 oak barriques under a dramatic central skylight. Above ground, a sharp ruby-red observation tower (la torre) commands 360-degree views over the Maremma plain.
notes: Subterranean Barricaia: Stepped amphitheater holding 2,500 barrels in concentric rows under a single light well.
The Red Tower: Renzo Piano's signature red steel observation tower framing the Tuscan horizon.
Acoustic & Thermal Stability: Deep underground embedment maintaining constant 15°C and 80% humidity.

field_studies_italy.title: Podere La Chiesa Winery
field_studies_italy.subtitle: Terricciola, Valdera (Near Borgo di Colleoli)
field_studies_italy.summary: Wednesday afternoon visit directly following the morning survey of Borgo di Colleoli. Located just kilometers from basecamp in Terricciola, Podere La Chiesa integrates contemporary winemaking inside an amphitheater-shaped cellar designed to host classical music concerts among fermentation vessels.
notes: Acoustic Tectonics: Elliptical subterranean tasting room designed for musical acoustics.
Proximity to Borgo: Valdera viticulture terroir directly adjacent to Colleoli.
Natural Light: Slotted apertures tracing sun angles onto aging oak casks.

field_studies_italy.title: Volterra Village & Historic Fabric
field_studies_italy.subtitle: Val di Cecina, Tuscany
field_studies_italy.typology: High-Altitude Hilltop Urbanism, Alabaster & Roman Theatre
field_studies_italy.summary: Wednesday field survey of the dramatic fortified hilltop settlement of Volterra. Sited dramatically on a windswept plateau 550 meters above the Cecina Valley, the town features 4th-century BC Etruscan cyclopean walls, a pristine 1st-century BC Roman theater, and towering medieval stone streetscapes.
notes: Plateau Morphology: Defensive edge conditions dropping precipitously into the 'Balze' ravines.
Etruscan Stone Joints: Massive dry-laid masonry surviving over 2,400 years.
Roman Theater: Calibrated acoustic bowl cut into the northern slope.

field_studies_italy.title: Villa Corsini a Mezzomonte
field_studies_italy.subtitle: Impruneta / San Casciano in Val di Pesa, Chianti
field_studies_italy.typology: Monumental Renaissance Villa Estate & Terraced Parterres
field_studies_italy.summary: Thursday morning countryside field trip prior to arriving in Florence. Once owned by Lorenzo the Magnificent and Cardinal Carlo de' Medici, Villa Corsini illustrates the classic Renaissance villa typology: axial walled formal gardens, vaulted fresco loggias, and panoramic agricultural vistas commanding the olive and vineyard slopes.
notes: Renaissance Villa Axis: Direct geometrical alignment between central salon, courtyard, and terraced parterres.
Microclimatic Loggias: Frescoed vaulted arcades providing passive cross-ventilation in summer.
Agrarian Integration: Formal geometric gardens dissolving into productive olive orchards.
